find: | Attestation verified? | yes / no / not attested (before 1.0) |
title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: A row missing from the checklist's template while the record still writes it: the two a person pastes side by side would no longer match.

title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: A field the workflow computes and the record does not list: applyPrior drops it silently and the run's issue never shows whether the attestation was verified.

find: | Previous version installed | (step 22: the version installed before this one, 0.1.0; none where step 22 was not run) |
title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: The update's field gone from the checklist's template while the record still writes it: a person run would not say which version it updated over.

title: is the results template's run table, row for row
why: A field the template has and the record does not list: the automated run's record would lack the row that says the update was not automated.

title: is the results template, row for row
why: Step 22 gone from the template's steps while the record still writes its row: the update over 0.1.0 would have nowhere to be recorded by a person.

title: names every step as its heading does, the time left blank there
why: Step 22 missing from the record: the automated run could not say it is not automated, and the record would claim twenty-one steps where the checklist has twenty-two.

title: answers from the tag's own file, true where it holds the text and false where not
why: Every tag that has the file read as holding the feature: a release from before the label is expected to report its -rc.N, and fails a row it passes.

title: answers null without a tag, for a tag this clone lacks, and without git
why: A tag the clone does not have read as one without the feature, so the App row is judged by the older rule instead of recorded as not checked.

title: answers false for a tag whose tree has no such file, and asks for no text
why: git's "no such path" read as git failing: a tag from before the file is recorded as not checked instead of judged by the older rule.

title: answers null when reading the file fails or times out, whatever it printed
why: A read that failed or timed out taken as the file: the tag is judged as one without the feature, on what git never finished printing.
